## 開篇固定收益主論點

投資人在7月消費者物價報告公布前不願延續週一的賣壓，美債8月11日小幅走高，即使油價再漲仍使能源衝擊受到關注。2年期殖利率下跌2.7個基點至4.216%，5年期下跌2.3個基點至4.39%，10年期回落1.8個基點至4.69%，30年期下滑1.1個基點至5.242%。短端漲勢較強，2年與10年期殖利率曲線擴大0.9個基點至47.4個基點，2年與30年期曲線擴大1.6個基點至102.6個基點。

這波漲勢不大，但在油價連漲五天後，其結構值得注意。10年期實質殖利率下跌0.7個基點至2.426%，10年期損益兩平通膨率也下降1.1個基點至2.264%。伊朗重申在其要求獲得滿足前，荷莫茲海峽將持續關閉，WTI上漲1.62%至$83.46，布蘭特原油上漲1.66%至$89.18。巴基斯坦表示美國與伊朗接近達成某種安排，卻未提出任何足以判斷一般航運何時能恢復的條件。

因此，美債市場並未把最新一波油價上漲視為整體通膨加速的充分證據。接下來應由CPI，而不是談判說法的再次變化，判斷能源衝擊是否與國內物價降溫同時發生。經濟學家預期7月整體CPI在6月下跌0.4%後，將上升0.1%。另有一項預測認為，能源項目將使月增幅減少11個基點，核心通膨年增率則會降至2021年3月以來最低；但這是回顧性的比較，尚未涵蓋最近油價反彈的全部影響。

部位配置使這項事件風險格外尖銳。UBS指出，截至7月底，商品交易顧問的全球債券減碼部位已較兩週前增為三倍；10年期殖利率每變動1個基點，其部位損益約為$3億，是UBS自1990年起資料中的最高敏感度。因此，若通膨結果溫和，趨勢追蹤交易者回補空單，漲勢可能超過一般數據公布日的幅度；若數據高於預期，則會強化既有的殖利率上升部位。

收盤結果顯示的是謹慎，而非全面防禦性撤出。標普500指數與那斯達克100指數均下跌約0.32%，費城半導體指數卻上漲0.87%。美元指數持平，VIX下跌1.16%至15.28，黃金期貨上漲1.52%至$4,428.20。投資級與高收益債券基金微幅收高，新興市場債券基金則幾乎持平。投資人略微壓低各天期債券殖利率，但沒有把尚未消除的通膨或地緣政治風險視為迫在眉睫的信用事件。

初級市場也呈現融資容量仍在、但投資人有所區別的相同訊號。洲際交易所發行$37.5億債券，為收購MarketAxess籌資，其中最長天期的利差較初步定價討論大幅收窄。Blue Owl吸引約$33億訂單後，將交易規模提高至$7.5億。信用條件較具挑戰的軟體公司Gainwell Technologies則推出$43.4億債券與貸款組合，初步需求約$40億，作為更全面資本結構重整的一環。

輝達帶來AI融資議題中最明確的新變化。執行長黃仁勳表示，對擬議中的$5,000億融資平台，輝達將逐案評估，對單一機會的支援上限為25%，而不是承諾自行出資支應整個標示金額。輝達2056年到期債券對美債利差收窄2個基點至113個基點，5年期信用違約交換利差最多收窄5個基點至72.11個基點。這項說明降低了輝達直接曝險的不確定性，但由舉債支持的AI建設如何轉化為可用產能與終端客戶報酬，這個更大的問題仍未解決。

## 美債在通膨考驗前守穩

美債的小幅上漲只收復週一部分跌幅。以一週計，2年期殖利率仍上升2.3個基點，5年期上升6.4個基點，10年期上升7.5個基點，30年期增加6.6個基點。拉長至一個月，分歧更加明顯：2年期幾乎持平，10年期上升12.8個基點，30年期則上升18.1個基點。週二由短端帶動的喘息，並未消除使長期殖利率維持在多年高檔附近的期限溢價。

市場調整期間，現券成交活躍。FINRA記錄的美債面額成交量達$1.03兆，較週一增加16.2%，共343,548筆交易。名目附息債券成交額增加13.3%至$7,906億。變化最大的是剩餘期限超過2年、但不超過3年的附息債券，成交額增加逾一倍至$1,592億，其中85.6%為最新發行券。這些數據衡量的是雙向成交量，而非投資人買賣方向，但顯示收盤走勢雖然溫和，政策敏感區段此前已經歷可觀的重新定價。

國內數據訊號不一。7月成屋銷售下降1.7%，折合年率為406萬戶，符合預測中位數；高房價與房貸利率繼續限制交易。全國獨立企業聯盟則表示，小型企業信心升至約一年來最高，計畫增聘員工的企業占比為2022年10月以來最高，企業回報的通膨疑慮則有所緩解。

這些數據仍無法釐清疲弱就業報告與新一波油價衝擊所形成的政策權衡。融資成本繼續壓抑房市，但小型企業調查並未顯示勞動需求全面崩跌，因此利率市場仍認為聯準會9月升息25個基點的機率接近五五波。CPI必須顯示能源以外的物價壓力是否足夠廣泛地降溫，能否抵銷企業更強的招募意向，以及燃料成本上漲最終擴散至服務業和商品配送的風險。

部位背景提高了CPI公布後第一波行情被放大的可能性。CTA管理的資產估計達$4,000億；在殖利率連月走高、油價高漲、貨幣政策緊縮預期及政府借款疑慮之下，它們已建立創紀錄的全球債券空單。UBS策略師Phoebe White表示，這類投資人進一步增持空單的空間有限，因此若債市上漲，被迫回補的潛在調整幅度，可能大於殖利率上升時新增的賣盤。

其他投資人對利率多頭觀點也已不再那麼堅定。摩根大通截至8月10日當週的調查顯示，客戶由做多轉為中立，淨多頭部位降至5月18日以來最低。美國銀行同樣發現CTA持有大量空單，尤以較短天期債券為甚。部位如此集中，使僅僅偏弱的整體數據與全面溫和的報告之間差異格外重要：即使整體數字符合預期，若結果主要受能源帶動、核心服務通膨仍具黏性，仍可能不足以促成持久的空單回補。

30年期債券另有結構性限制。巴克萊估計，在聯準會與外國央行的相對占比下降後，民間投資人目前持有73%的美債，高於十年前約50%。共同基金、家庭、銀行與外國民間投資人通常要求價格足以補償其預期報酬，而非主要出於政策或外匯存底管理目的買進。

這項轉變恰逢2007年以來30年期殖利率在5%以上維持最久的一段期間。截至週二，該殖利率已連續41個交易日高於5%，收盤仍為5.242%。彭博一項20年以上到期美債指數繼2025年上漲4.6%後，今年已下跌3.8%。持續的通膨、擴大的財政赤字，以及民間買方必須承接的大量利率風險，使長端對單一疲弱就業報告或損益兩平通膨率一日小幅下降的反應，弱於短天期債券。

週二的殖利率拆解確實帶來有限緩解。10年期實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率均告下降，不同於週一實質利率走高、通膨補償增加的組合。不過，變動幅度不足以扭轉全週趨勢，10年期實質殖利率仍較一週前高3.9個基點。市場只是在通膨數據公布前暫停，尚未認定近期賣壓背後的實質利率或通膨風險已經化解。

## 荷莫茲不確定性延長油價與新興市場衝擊

盤中各方的外交說法更加矛盾。美國總統川普擴大對伊朗的要求，納入向德黑蘭相關攻擊及伊朗國內抗議中的死者提供賠償。伊朗先前也已就其所稱美國違反臨時和平安排之舉要求賠償。雙方要求轉趨強硬，降低了談判迅速形成彼此接受的荷莫茲海峽重開條件之可能性。

巴基斯坦國防部長Khawaja Asif提出較樂觀的說法，稱雙方接近達成某種安排，局勢正朝和平發展。巴基斯坦一直擔任調停者，但Asif沒有提出取得突破的證據。油價一度因可能出現進展的說法而反應，隨後在伊朗官員重申其條件獲得滿足前航道仍將關閉後反轉。

實體運輸受阻的程度，仍遠大於外交新聞標題所暗示的情況。美國能源資訊署估計，第2季經荷莫茲海峽運送的石油平均每日490萬桶，低於戰爭爆發前、2025年第4季的2,160萬桶。該署預期，約每日60萬桶的衝突相關供應中斷將延續至2027年底，並分別上調2026年汽油與柴油價格預測3.7%和5.4%，2027年零售汽油價格預測也較前月提高6.5%。

這些預測並不表示油價每天上漲都會直接傳導至消費者通膨，卻把供應問題的時間拉長至下一次聯準會會議之後。經海峽運送的油量減少與產量直接損失也必須區分：即使部分原油最終仍能送達買方，通行受限也會推高運費、保險與交付成本；若產量本身持續無法供應，煉油商與消費者面對的則是另一種更深的衝擊。

新興市場比美國信用市場更直接反映這類曝險。開發中經濟體貨幣報酬指數下跌0.1%，南非與匈牙利等能源進口國承壓。菲律賓披索出現5月以來最大跌幅，韓元則是少數走強的貨幣之一。印度央行進場支撐盧比之際，印度股債表現落後。

能源衝擊與極端天候疊加，使東歐多地公債殖利率上升。乾旱正對區域電力與農業系統造成壓力，羅馬尼亞警告，多瑙河流量降至歷史新低，可能迫使切爾納沃德核電廠關閉第2座反應爐。德國萊茵河在考布附近最淺處的水位，則降至1880年有紀錄以來最低，妨礙這條對歐洲工業至關重要的運輸路線。這些是區域供應限制，而非美國通膨數據造成的結果，但仍增加了能源與食品成本可能持續偏高的傳導管道。

美國風險性資產並未呈現相同程度的壓力。標普500指數下跌0.3%，公用事業、能源與工業類股上漲，大型科技公司則拖累指數。布蘭特原油升破$89，令先前因荷莫茲協議即將達成的說法而更為樂觀的投資人失望，但波動率並未出現同等程度的飆升，上市信用債基金也未普遍惡化。

美元收盤持平之際，黃金期貨上漲，油價走高，美債殖利率則略降。這種組合較符合投資人因衝突未解及CPI事件風險而尋求保護，而非單純押注成長或通膨。跨市場結果仍留下兩項不同的考驗：國內通膨將決定近期聯準會政策路徑；實際航運能否恢復，則決定能源是否不再反覆成為物價壓力來源。

## 信用市場承接併購與AI融資

輝達對$5,000億融資計畫的說明改變了市場對其信用風險的評估，卻沒有降低AI潛在借款規模。該公司正與Apollo、Blackstone、BlackRock、Brookfield、高盛及KKR合作，為購買運算能力的客戶建立第三方資本池。擬議債務可採私募或透過特殊目的機構發行，以輝達運算設備作為抵押，再將設備出租給客戶。

單一融資載體每次可能發行數百億美元，交易最快可能在數月內進入市場。輝達對合格單一機會的支援最高可達25%，但黃仁勳將其描述為有限度、以殘值為依據，且僅作為獨立授信審查的補充。這項差異相當重要：輝達是在協助建立抵押品價值與融資能力，並非承諾負擔整個$5,000億標示金額的四分之一。

債券投資人對潛在義務範圍縮小作出正面反應。輝達票息5.625%、2056年到期債券對可比美債利差收窄至113個基點，5年期信用違約交換利差最多下降5個基點。這項反應部分扭轉了最初公布計畫時的不確定性，當時交易時程、結構及輝達自身資產負債表曝險均不清楚。

然而，這個平台只是轉移、而非消除底層專案風險。運算設備可以轉供其他買方，使貸款人的回收彈性優於為沒有其他用途的單一目的資產融資。但晶片可以移轉，不代表資料中心一定能按時取得土地、電力、變壓器及監管許可，也不能證明超大規模雲端服務商與其他終端使用者能迅速取得足以支撐上游投資規模的報酬。

這種經濟錯配仍是AI信用風險的核心。晶片製造商目前取得價值鏈中最優厚的利潤，較接近終端使用者的公司則仍在設法把大型投資計畫轉化為可擴張的獲利。私募資本可以填補基礎設施支出與收入實現之間的空檔，但持續再融資取決於受融資資產的現金產生能力、使用年限及可移轉性。輝達限制直接支援，降低了自身債權人的集中風險，專案層級的授信問題則仍由參與的貸款人與債券持有人承擔。

傳統高評級市場繼續展現承接深度。洲際交易所在宣布以$60億收購MarketAxess後不到兩週，完成四期、期限介於3至10年的固定利率債券定價，總額$37.5億。最長一期以美債加82個基點定價，初步討論水準約為加115個基點。浮動利率一期在承銷過程中取消，整體固定利率交易規模則超過借款人最初尋求的約$35億。

定價顯示，只要債券最初提供足夠利差，投資人願意為這筆讓洲際交易所掌控主要固定收益交易平台的收購案提供資金。洲際交易所已向美國銀行安排最高$62.5億的過橋融資，因此這次債券發行是以定期債務取代部分臨時資金。美國銀行與富國銀行擔任主動簿記管理人。

週二共有10家投資級發行人籌得$166億，洲際交易所是其中之一；前一天則有19家公司集中發債。其他併購融資包括Martin Marietta Materials發行$55億債券，為擬以$135億收購Lhoist North America籌資，以及Ferguson Enterprises在同意收購FWI Holdings後完成$12億交易。CPI公布前供給因而維持高檔，但結構完善的交易仍能在行銷期間收窄利差。

Blue Owl Capital同樣獲得大量需求，把10年期發行規模由初步討論的$5億提高至$7.5億。訂單高峰約達$33億後，該債券以美債加220個基點定價，較初步指引收窄約30個基點。募集資金將用於償還循環信用借款，Blue Owl Capital等12個實體列為保證人。

這份較強的訂單簿出現在市場一度擔憂上市信用基金之後，但Blue Owl表示，借款人基本面依然穩健，市場對AI相關顛覆的疑慮也已開始緩解。其利差仍遠高於最大型工業企業或交易所業者可取得的水準，顯示需求並非不區分商業模式或產業。投資人是在殖利率足以補償風險的情況下，接受這家私募信貸管理公司的信用風險。

Gainwell的交易則是更嚴格的槓桿融資考驗。這家政府醫療軟體供應商推出5年期高收益債券，納入總額$43.4億、另含槓桿貸款的融資組合。連同修改並延長一筆$14.6億第二順位定期貸款，這些交易旨在透過規模更廣的$58億重整，為公司整體資本結構再融資。

截至週二，債券與貸款組合已取得約$40億訂單，兩個新組成部分預計本週稍晚完成。軟體借款人正面臨AI顛覆既有產品與收入的疑慮，Gainwell必須在此背景下完成再融資。其他情況相近、由私募股權持有的公司近期必須支付更高成本並接受較短展期，包括Proofpoint在7月一筆$43億交易中作出重大讓步。

Gainwell進入融資程序時，營運結果正在改善。截至6月止一季，營收由一年前的$4.93億增至$5.26億，調整後息稅折舊攤銷前盈餘則由$8,700萬升至$9,300萬。重整計畫公布後，穆迪將公司評級由Caa1調升一級；標普也把它列入可能升評的觀察名單，理由是交易可處理即將到期的債務並改善流動性。新債評級預計落在單B級，可把潛在買方擴大至因限制而不能持有CCC級債券的基金以外。

市政借款人也增加供給。亞特蘭大市為改善哈茲菲爾德—傑克遜國際機場，發行約$10.9億債券，其中約$6.99億適用替代性最低稅，$3.91億免受該稅影響。部分2036年7月到期的AMT債券，初步水準顯示票息5%、殖利率3.84%，約高於基準60個基點。債券評級屬AA級，資金將用於擴建D航廈、增加達美航空貴賓室空間及興建停車設施。

相較於清淡的機場債發行日程，這筆交易規模龐大。今年機場類市政債發行額接近$100億，較2025年同期低約28%；當年多項十億美元級計畫使全年銷售額增至近$240億。亞特蘭大預期2033年登機旅客將較2019年增加110%，並計畫在2032年前為資本支出方案再發行$37億債務。本次債券為基礎設施提供即時資金，未來發債時程則使投資人必須一併評估旅客成長與新增槓桿的發展。

## 全球央行面對不同形式的通膨壓力

亞洲與新興市場的政策訊號，持續依各自國內通膨、成長及油價曝險而分歧。韓國央行第一副總裁Ryoo Sangdai表示，如果強勁成長繼續推升基礎通膨，可能還需要進一步升息；這番談話在8月27日會議前強化了央行的緊縮傾向。

Ryoo是七名理事會成員之一，任期將於8月20日屆滿。他表示，升息時點與步調將取決於後續數據及央行更新後的預測。韓元回穩及南韓股市下跌為決策者帶來一些彈性，但他更重視核心通膨是否維持高檔、成長動能是否延續，以及金融穩定風險是否加劇。

韓國央行7月將基準利率上調25個基點至2.75%，是2023年初以來首次升息。此後整體通膨降至2.8%，但仍高於2%目標；核心通膨則微升至2.6%。第2季經濟成長0.6%，高於預期，7月按工作日調整的出口較一年前成長近70%。Ryoo表示，通膨或許不會重演俄羅斯入侵烏克蘭後的飆升，但半導體榮景可能支撐薪資與消費，使幅度較小的物價漲勢持續。

澳洲央行採取不同選擇，連續第二次會議把現金利率維持在4.35%。決策者寄望失業率上升與房市轉弱能充分抑制經濟活動，進而使通膨降溫；通膨約五年來一直未回到2%至3%目標區間的中點。不過，總裁Michele Bullock表示進一步緊縮仍很有可能，即使部分分析師認為升息循環大概已經結束，央行仍保留偏鷹派的政策選項。

巴西央行會議紀要一方面延續降息，另一方面警告政策必須保持限制性。央行在8月5日會議把Selic利率下調25個基點至14%，為連續第四次降息，自3月以來累計寬鬆100個基點。決策者表示，緊縮政策抑制經濟活動的證據持續增加，但供需衝擊仍在造成通膨。

7月消費者物價年增率降至4.44%，略高於4.4%的預測中位數，月增率為0.07%。食品飲料價格下跌0.67%，服飾下跌0.66%，住宅成本則上升0.99%。央行相關政策期間所指的2028年第1季通膨預期仍高於3%目標，央行調查的經濟學家則預期2028年底通膨率為3.8%。

會議紀要強調，通膨預期失去錨定，意味政策必須比原本所需更長時間維持緊縮。央行也把油價波動及聖嬰現象相關食品風險列為可能引發第二輪效應的來源。高盛經濟學家Alberto Ramos認為，9月中旬會議仍可能再次降息，但近期大幅寬鬆的空間有限。

肯亞連續第三次會議把基準利率維持在8.75%，符合調查中五項預測。總裁Kamau Thugge表示，此一政策立場旨在讓通膨預期維持於2.5%至7.5%的目標區間內，並穩定匯率。央行的短期通膨預測假設中東衝突降溫，因此政策展望直接取決於一項截至美國收盤時仍未發生的情勢。

肯亞7月通膨率由6.4%升至6.5%，核心通膨則由3.1%增至3.2%，反映燃料成本上漲擴散至食品與運輸。玉米歉收及強烈聖嬰現象的可能性也增加國內供應風險。央行表示，將監控油價與第二輪效應，並準備在必要時採取行動。

菲律賓同時面臨財政供給增加與進口能源曝險。政府計畫2027年舉債3.3兆披索，約合$540億，較今年修訂後的2.73兆披索計畫增加約20%。借款將支應擬議7.2兆披索預算的46%，該預算較目前配置高6%。

國內發債規模規劃為2.39兆披索，增加24%，約占總借款72%。政府預計向包含多邊貸款機構在內的海外債權人籌得9,150億披索，其中國際債券為3,660億披索，高於今年的3,144億披索。菲律賓2026年迄今已發行$52.5億全球債券。

財政赤字預估為1.69兆披索，占GDP的5.1%，高於先前4.8%的目標。6月未償債務為19.07兆披索，約占GDP的66%。伊朗戰爭與國內貪腐醜聞削弱成長後，總統小馬可仕正增加基礎建設與社會支出，並提供家庭稅務減免及能源補貼。今年當地債券以美元避險計算已虧損5%，披索也下跌3.7%；規模更大的供給計畫因而必須與通膨及匯率風險爭取資金。

日圓再次貶向1美元兌160日圓，重新引發干預揣測，但政策限制並未實質改變。日圓已回吐7月31日美日協調行動後漲幅的近一半。日本央行利率為1%，聯準會目標區間則為3.5%至3.75%；利差、日本財政前景及進口能源成本上升，仍與官方偏好日圓走強的方向相抵觸。

## 市場前瞻意義

週三公布的7月CPI，是美債漲勢面臨的立即考驗。預測中位數為月增0.1%，前月則下跌0.4%；另有預測認為，能源項目將使月增幅減少11個基點，核心通膨年增率會降至2021年3月以來最低。若各分項普遍溫和，國內通膨降溫將與疲弱就業訊號相互印證，並可能迫使持有創紀錄債券空單的CTA回補。若結果主要受先前能源價格下跌帶動，核心服務壓力仍持續，市場就較缺乏理由放棄9月升息預期。

實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率各自的變動也很重要。即使油價上漲，10年期名目殖利率的這兩項組成部分週二都下降。若CPI結構溫和，預期政策路徑與通膨補償可望同時降低，延續這波緩解；若各分項普遍高於預期，則會挑戰實質殖利率的降勢，並顯示能源衝擊來臨時，國內持續性通膨尚未充分消退。

荷莫茲海峽需要的是實際運作證據，而非又一次談判取得進展的說法。具持久性的改變應包括各方接受的通行條件、重開時間表、足以供商業使用者運作的交通量，以及能讓一般貨運恢復的保險條件。儘管巴基斯坦態度樂觀，伊朗仍堅持海峽繼續關閉，顯示這些條件尚未達成。第2季平均通行油量由戰前每日2,160萬桶降至490萬桶，為市場判斷任何協議成效提供了實體基準。

週四$250億的30年期美債標售，將在市場殖利率約5.24%、且已連續41個交易日高於5%的背景下考驗需求。巴克萊預期，由於民間且價格敏感的投資人在買方結構中占比提高，市場會長期要求更多補償，以承擔通膨、財政赤字及長天期債券供給。標售殖利率、投標分布及之後的交易，將顯示目前水準能否吸引足夠買盤，或仍須提供更大讓利。

Gainwell的債券與貸款預計本週稍晚完成。投資人一面評估AI顛覆、整體資本結構再融資及營運改善的價值，約$40億初步訂單則必須轉化為$43.4億融資組合的最終定價。若無須大幅削弱條件便能完成，將證明市場有能力承接單B級軟體借款人；若規模縮小或讓步擴大，則會強化槓桿科技融資市場已顯現的選擇性。

輝達逐步成形的融資載體，是一項更長期的信用考驗。公司已說明，自身對單一機會的支援上限為25%，但首批交易仍須確立槓桿、抵押權、客戶義務，以及過時或重新配置運算設備的處理方式。特殊目的發行人能否籌得數百億美元，不只取決於輝達提供的殘值支援，也取決於實體建設與商業報酬追上資本承諾之前，專案現金流是否足以償債。

韓國央行8月27日會議將決定，持續偏高的核心通膨、強勁出口及高於預期的成長，是否足以支持央行在7月升息至2.75%後再次升息。更新後的成長與通膨預測格外重要，因為Ryoo已把緊縮的時點與步調繫於這些資訊。澳洲、巴西與肯亞也各自保留附帶條件的政策傾向，但在近期決策中，韓國的再次升息已是現行選項，而非等壓力重現後才可能採取的遙遠因應。

overall_summary.headline: 油價再漲之際，美債在CPI公布前小幅走高
overall_summary.session_narrative:
儘管油價連續第五天上漲，投資人在7月CPI公布前暫停加碼賣出，美債8月11日小幅走高。2年期殖利率下跌2.7個基點至4.216%，10年期回落1.8個基點至4.69%，30年期下降1.1個基點至5.242%，殖利率曲線因而轉陡。10年期實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率均下滑，顯示市場當天並未全面轉向更高通膨的定價。

市場走勢克制，反映國內物價與能源供應皆有不確定性。經濟學家預期7月整體CPI在前月下跌0.4%後上升0.1%，而創紀錄的全球債券空單可能放大市場反應。伊朗堅稱其要求獲得滿足前荷莫茲海峽將持續關閉，即使巴基斯坦聲稱協議已經接近，油價仍然上漲；海峽通行量也已較戰前水準大幅下降。

信用市場繼續選擇性承接大型交易。洲際交易所發行$37.5億併購融資債券，Blue Owl在需求強勁後提高發行規模，Gainwell則推出難度更高的$43.4億再融資組合。輝達說明，對擬議AI融資平台的支援將以單一機會為準、上限為25%，而非負擔$5,000億的標示總額，消息帶動其債券走強。
overall_summary.summary: 投資人等待7月CPI，沒有因油價上漲及荷莫茲海峽運輸持續受阻，就認定國內通膨正在加速；美債殖利率因而由短端領跌，溫和下降。

section_summaries.summary: 強勁成長與核心通膨持續之際，韓國央行維持緊縮傾向；澳洲則按兵不動，但仍可能進一步緊縮。巴西繼續逐步降息，同時警告通膨預期失去錨定需要政策更長時間保持限制性；肯亞維持利率的判斷則部分取決於衝突降溫。菲律賓借款增加與日圓再度走弱，也加重財政、匯率及進口能源壓力。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries edged higher on Aug. 11 even as another rise in oil kept the energy shock in view, with investors reluctant to extend Monday’s selloff before the July consumer-price report. The 2-year yield declined 2.7 basis points to 4.216%, the 5-year fell 2.3 basis points to 4.39%, the 10-year eased 1.8 basis points to 4.69% and the 30-year slipped 1.1 basis points to 5.242%. The stronger move at the front end widened the 2s10s curve by 0.9 basis point to 47.4 basis points and 2s30s by 1.6 basis points to 102.6 basis points.

The rally was modest, but its composition was notable after oil extended a five-day advance. The 10-year real yield fell 0.7 basis point to 2.426%, while the 10-year breakeven declined 1.1 basis points to 2.264%. WTI rose 1.62% to $83.46 and Brent gained 1.66% to $89.18 as Iran reiterated that the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until its demands were met. Pakistan said the US and Iran were close to some form of arrangement, but offered no terms that would establish when ordinary shipping could resume.

Treasuries therefore did not treat the latest increase in crude as sufficient evidence of a broader inflation acceleration. The coming CPI release, rather than another swing in negotiating rhetoric, was left to determine whether the energy shock is occurring alongside moderation in domestic prices. Economists expect headline CPI to rise 0.1% in July after a 0.4% decline in June. One forecast expects energy to subtract 11 basis points from the monthly result and core annual inflation to reach its lowest level since March 2021, a backward-looking comparison that does not capture the full effect of the latest oil rebound.

Positioning made that event risk unusually acute. Commodity trading advisers had tripled their underweight global-bond positions by the end of July from two weeks earlier, according to UBS. Their exposure was equivalent to about $300 million of profit or loss for every 1-basis-point move in 10-year yields, the largest sensitivity in UBS data extending to 1990. A benign inflation result could consequently produce more than a routine data-day rally if trend followers cover shorts, while an upside surprise would reinforce positions already aligned with rising yields.

The completed close showed caution rather than broad defensive liquidation. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 each lost about 0.32%, but the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 0.87%. The dollar index was unchanged, the VIX fell 1.16% to 15.28 and gold futures rose 1.52% to $4,428.20. Investment-grade and high-yield bond funds finished fractionally higher, while the emerging-market debt fund was almost unchanged. Investors were marking down duration yields slightly without treating unresolved inflation or geopolitical risk as an immediate credit event.

Primary markets gave a similar signal of capacity coupled with discrimination. Intercontinental Exchange sold $3.75 billion of bonds to finance its MarketAxess acquisition, tightening the longest tranche substantially from initial price discussions. Blue Owl increased a deal to $750 million after attracting about $3.3 billion of orders. Gainwell Technologies, a more difficult software credit, launched a $4.34 billion bond-and-loan package with roughly $4 billion of preliminary demand as part of a broader overhaul of its capital structure.

Nvidia supplied the clearest change in the AI-financing story. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang said the company’s support for a proposed $500 billion financing platform would be limited to as much as 25% of an individual opportunity, assessed project by project, rather than representing an obligation to fund the headline amount itself. Nvidia’s 2056 bond spread narrowed 2 basis points to 113 basis points over Treasuries, while its 5-year credit-default swap narrowed as much as 5 basis points to 72.11 basis points. The clarification reduced uncertainty about Nvidia’s direct exposure even as it left the much larger question of how debt-financed AI construction will translate into usable capacity and end-customer returns unresolved.

## Treasuries Hold Their Ground Before the Inflation Test

The small Treasury rally reversed only part of Monday’s selloff. Over one week, the 2-year yield remained 2.3 basis points higher, the 5-year was up 6.4 basis points, the 10-year had risen 7.5 basis points and the 30-year had added 6.6 basis points. Over one month, the divergence was wider: the 2-year was almost unchanged, while the 10-year had risen 12.8 basis points and the 30-year 18.1 basis points. Tuesday’s front-end-led relief did not remove the term premium that has kept long yields near multiyear extremes.

Cash-market turnover was heavy during the adjustment. FINRA recorded $1.03 trillion of Treasury par activity, 16.2% more than on Monday, across 343,548 trades. Nominal-coupon activity increased 13.3% to $790.6 billion. The largest reported change was in coupons with more than 2 years and no more than 3 years to maturity, where activity more than doubled to $159.2 billion and 85.6% involved on-the-run securities. The data measure two-way turnover rather than investor direction, but they show that the modest closing move followed substantial repricing activity in the policy-sensitive sector.

The market had mixed domestic evidence to process. Existing-home sales fell 1.7% in July to an annualized 4.06 million, matching the median forecast, as high prices and mortgage rates continued to constrain transactions. The National Federation of Independent Business said small-business optimism rose to its highest in roughly a year. The share of firms planning to add workers reached its highest since October 2022, while reported inflation concerns eased.

Those releases did not settle the policy balance exposed by the weak employment report and renewed oil shock. Housing remained restrained by financing costs, but the small-business survey did not describe a generalized collapse in labor demand. Interest-rate markets were consequently still assigning close to even odds to a quarter-point Fed increase in September. The CPI result must show whether easing price pressure outside energy is sufficiently broad to outweigh stronger hiring intentions and the risk that higher fuel costs eventually spread into services and goods distribution.

The positioning backdrop increases the chance that the first move after CPI will be amplified. CTAs manage an estimated $400 billion and have already built record global-bond shorts after months of rising yields, high oil prices, expectations of tighter monetary policy and concern about government borrowing. UBS strategist Phoebe White said the group had limited room to add further shorts, making forced covering on a rally a larger prospective adjustment than incremental selling if yields rise.

Other investors have also become less committed to a bullish rates view. JPMorgan’s weekly survey showed clients moving to neutral from long in the week through Aug. 10, leaving the net long position at its smallest since May 18. Bank of America likewise found CTAs heavily short, particularly in shorter-dated notes. That concentration makes the distinction between a merely soft headline and a broadly benign report important: an energy-driven result with sticky core services could fail to trigger durable covering even if the headline meets expectations.

The 30-year sector faces a separate structural constraint. Barclays estimates that private investors now hold 73% of the Treasury market, compared with roughly 50% a decade ago, after the Federal Reserve and foreign central banks reduced their relative presence. Mutual funds, households, banks and foreign private investors generally require prices that compensate them for expected returns, rather than buying principally for policy or reserve-management purposes.

That shift has coincided with the longest sustained period of 30-year yields above 5% since 2007. The yield had spent 41 trading days above that threshold through Tuesday and remained at 5.242% at the close. A Bloomberg index of Treasuries with maturities longer than 20 years had lost 3.8% this year after gaining 4.6% in 2025. Persistent inflation, larger fiscal deficits and the volume of duration that private buyers must absorb have made the long end less responsive than short maturities to a single weak labor report or a modest daily decline in breakevens.

Tuesday’s yield decomposition did offer limited relief. Both the 10-year real yield and breakeven inflation declined, unlike Monday’s combination of higher real rates and greater inflation compensation. Yet the moves were too small to overturn the weekly pattern, and the 10-year real yield was still 3.9 basis points higher than a week earlier. The market had paused before inflation data; it had not concluded that the real-rate or inflation risks behind the recent selloff were resolved.

## Hormuz Uncertainty Extends the Oil and Emerging-Market Shock

The diplomatic account became more contradictory during the session. President Donald Trump had expanded his demands on Iran to include reparations for people killed in attacks linked to Tehran and in domestic protests. Iran had already sought compensation for what it described as US violations of an interim peace arrangement. The hardening claims reduced the likelihood that talks would quickly produce mutually accepted terms for reopening Hormuz.

Pakistan’s Defense Minister Khawaja Asif offered a more optimistic account, saying the parties were close to some sort of arrangement and that developments were moving in favor of peace. Pakistan has been acting as a mediator, but Asif supplied no evidence of a breakthrough. Oil briefly responded to the suggestion of progress before reversing as Iranian officials repeated that the waterway would remain closed until their conditions were satisfied.

The physical disruption remained far larger than the diplomatic headlines implied. The US Energy Information Administration estimated that oil transported through Hormuz averaged 4.9 million barrels a day in Q2, down from 21.6 million in the final quarter of 2025 before the war began. The administration expects conflict-related supply disruptions of about 600,000 barrels a day to persist through the end of 2027. It raised its 2026 gasoline and diesel price forecasts by 3.7% and 5.4%, respectively, and increased its 2027 retail-gasoline forecast by 6.5% from the previous month.

Those projections do not establish that every daily oil advance will pass directly into consumer inflation, but they extend the horizon of the supply problem well beyond the next Fed meeting. The distinction between barrels moving through the strait and outright lost production also matters. Restricted traffic raises freight, insurance and delivery costs even when some crude ultimately reaches buyers, while refiners and consumers face a different shock if production itself remains unavailable.

Emerging markets reflected that exposure more directly than US credit. An index of developing-economy currency returns fell 0.1%, with energy importers including South Africa and Hungary under pressure. The Philippine peso posted its largest decline since May, while the South Korean won was one of the few stronger currencies. Indian stocks and bonds lagged as the Reserve Bank of India intervened to support the rupee.

Government-bond yields rose across much of eastern Europe as the energy shock combined with extreme weather. Drought was straining regional power and agricultural systems, and Romania warned that record-low flows in the Danube could force the shutdown of a second reactor at the Cernavoda nuclear plant. In Germany, water at the Rhine’s shallowest point near Kaub had fallen to the lowest level in records dating to 1880, impairing a transport route central to European industry. These were regional supply constraints rather than consequences of US inflation data, but they added channels through which energy and food costs could persist.

US risk assets did not register the same degree of strain. The S&P 500 fell 0.3%, with utilities, energy and industrial shares advancing while large technology companies weighed on the index. Brent’s move above $89 disappointed investors who had responded more enthusiastically to earlier claims that a Hormuz agreement was imminent, but there was no comparable surge in volatility or broad deterioration in listed credit funds.

Gold futures rose even as the dollar finished unchanged, while oil gained and Treasury yields declined slightly. That combination was consistent with demand for protection against the unresolved conflict and event risk surrounding CPI, rather than a simple growth or inflation trade. The cross-market outcome left two distinct tests in place: domestic inflation must determine the near-term Fed path, while operational shipping access must determine whether energy can cease being a recurring source of price pressure.

## Credit Markets Absorb Acquisition and AI Financing

Nvidia’s clarification changed the credit assessment of its $500 billion financing initiative without reducing the prospective scale of AI borrowing. The company is working with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to create pools of third-party capital for customers acquiring computing capacity. Proposed debt could be issued privately or through special-purpose vehicles, with Nvidia compute pledged as collateral and the equipment leased to customers.

Individual vehicles could issue tens of billions of dollars at a time, and transactions may begin reaching the market within months. Support from Nvidia could amount to as much as 25% of a qualifying opportunity, but Huang described that support as limited, based on residual value and supplementary to independent underwriting. The difference is material: Nvidia is helping establish collateral value and financing capacity, not promising to fund one-quarter of the entire $500 billion headline.

Bond investors responded to the narrower potential obligation. Nvidia’s 5.625% notes due in 2056 tightened to 113 basis points over comparable Treasuries, and its 5-year credit-default swap fell as much as 5 basis points. The reaction reversed some uncertainty created by the initial announcement, when timing, structure and Nvidia’s own balance-sheet exposure were unclear.

The platform nevertheless transfers rather than eliminates the underlying project risks. Compute can be redeployed to another buyer, giving lenders more recovery flexibility than financing a single-purpose asset with no secondary use. The ability to move chips does not guarantee that data centers will obtain land, power, transformers and regulatory approval on schedule. Nor does it establish that hyperscalers and other end users will earn returns rapidly enough to support the volume of upstream investment.

That economic mismatch remains central to AI credit. Chipmakers have been earning the strongest margins in the value chain, while companies closer to the final users are still trying to turn large investment programs into scalable profit. Private capital can bridge the period between infrastructure spending and realized revenue, but continued refinancing depends on the cash generation, useful life and portability of the financed assets. Nvidia’s limitation of its direct support reduced concentration risk for its own creditors while leaving those project-level underwriting questions with the participating lenders and bondholders.

The conventional high-grade market continued to show depth. ICE priced $3.75 billion of fixed-rate notes in four tranches with maturities from 3 to 10 years, less than two weeks after announcing its $6 billion acquisition of MarketAxess. The longest tranche priced at 82 basis points over Treasuries, compared with initial discussion around 115 basis points. A floating-rate tranche was dropped during syndication, while the overall fixed-rate transaction exceeded the roughly $3.5 billion the borrower had initially sought.

The pricing showed that investors were willing to finance an acquisition that will give ICE control of a major fixed-income trading platform, provided the bonds offered enough initial spread. ICE had arranged as much as $6.25 billion of bridge financing from Bank of America, so the bond sale replaces part of temporary funding with term debt. Bank of America and Wells Fargo served as active managers.

ICE was one of 10 investment-grade issuers that raised a combined $16.6 billion on Tuesday, following the previous day’s 19-company rush. Other acquisition financings included Martin Marietta Materials’ $5.5 billion sale for its planned $13.5 billion purchase of Lhoist North America and Ferguson Enterprises’ $1.2 billion transaction after its agreement to acquire FWI Holdings. The sequence kept supply elevated ahead of CPI without preventing well-structured deals from tightening during marketing.

Blue Owl Capital also found substantial demand, increasing a 10-year offering to $750 million from initial discussions of $500 million. The note priced at 220 basis points over Treasuries, about 30 basis points tighter than initial indications, after peak orders reached approximately $3.3 billion. Proceeds will repay revolving-credit borrowings, and a dozen entities, including Blue Owl Capital, are listed as guarantors.

The stronger orderbook followed a period of concern about publicly listed credit funds, but Blue Owl said borrower fundamentals remained solid and that anxiety about AI-related disruption had begun to ease. The spread remained much wider than those available to the largest industrial or exchange borrowers, showing that demand was not indifferent to business model or sector. Investors accepted the private-credit manager’s risk at a yield that compensated them for it.

Gainwell’s transaction provided a more demanding leveraged-finance test. The government-health-software provider launched a 5-year high-yield bond as part of a $4.34 billion package that also includes a leveraged loan. Together with the amendment and extension of a $1.46 billion second-lien term loan, the transactions are intended to refinance the company’s entire capital structure in a broader $5.8 billion overhaul.

Approximately $4 billion of orders had been submitted for the bond and loan package by Tuesday, with both new components expected to finish later in the week. Gainwell must refinance while software borrowers face concern that artificial intelligence will disrupt existing products and revenue. Comparable private-equity-owned companies have recently been required to pay more and accept shorter extensions, including Proofpoint, which made significant concessions on a $4.3 billion deal in July.

Gainwell entered the process with improving operating results. Revenue increased to $526 million in the quarter through June from $493 million a year earlier, while adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization rose to $93 million from $87 million. Moody’s upgraded the company one notch from Caa1 after the overhaul was announced, and S&P placed it on watch for a possible upgrade because the transaction could address approaching maturities and improve liquidity. Ratings on the new bond were expected to fall within the single-B category, broadening the potential buyer base beyond funds constrained from holding CCC debt.

Municipal borrowers also added supply. Atlanta offered about $1.09 billion for improvements at Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport, including roughly $699 million subject to the alternative-minimum tax and $391 million exempt from it. Preliminary levels for some AMT bonds due in July 2036 indicated a 3.84% yield on a 5% coupon, about 60 basis points above the benchmark. The debt carries AA-category ratings and will finance a Concourse D expansion, additional Delta lounge space and a parking facility.

The sale is large relative to a subdued airport calendar. Airport-sector municipal issuance was running near $10 billion for the year, about 28% below the comparable 2025 level, when several billion-dollar projects lifted total sales to almost $24 billion. Atlanta expects a 110% increase in enplaned passengers by 2033 from 2019 and plans another $3.7 billion of debt for its capital program through 2032. The immediate bond provides infrastructure funding, while the future issuance schedule leaves investors assessing how traffic growth and additional leverage develop together.

## Global Central Banks Confront Different Forms of Inflation Pressure

Asia and emerging-market policy signals remained divided according to domestic inflation, growth and exposure to oil. Bank of Korea Senior Deputy Governor Ryoo Sangdai said further rate increases would probably be needed if strong growth continued to feed underlying inflation, reinforcing the bank’s tightening bias before its Aug. 27 meeting.

Ryoo, whose term as one of the seven board members ends Aug. 20, said the timing and pace would depend on incoming data and the bank’s revised forecasts. The stabilization of the won and a decline in South Korean equities gave policymakers some flexibility, but he placed greater weight on whether core inflation remained elevated, whether growth momentum persisted and whether financial-stability risks intensified.

The BOK raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 2.75% in July, its first increase since early 2023. Headline inflation subsequently eased to 2.8%, still above the 2% target, while core inflation edged up to 2.6%. Q2 growth exceeded expectations at 0.6%, and working-day-adjusted exports rose almost 70% from a year earlier in July. Ryoo said inflation might not repeat the surge that followed Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, but the semiconductor boom could sustain wages and consumption, keeping a smaller increase in prices persistent.

Australia’s central bank made a different choice, holding its cash rate at 4.35% for a second consecutive meeting. Policymakers are relying on higher unemployment and a weakening property market to slow activity sufficiently to cool inflation, which has not returned to the midpoint of the 2%-to-3% target range for about five years. Governor Michele Bullock nevertheless said further tightening remained quite possible, preserving a hawkish contingency even as some analysts judged that the increase cycle was probably complete.

Brazil’s central bank minutes balanced continued easing with a warning that policy must stay restrictive. At its Aug. 5 meeting, the bank cut the Selic rate by 25 basis points to 14%, its fourth consecutive reduction and the 100th basis point of cumulative easing since March. Policymakers said evidence that tight policy was restraining activity had continued to accumulate, but demand and supply shocks were still generating inflation.

Annual consumer-price inflation eased to 4.44% in July, slightly above the 4.4% median forecast, with a monthly increase of 0.07%. Food and beverage prices fell 0.67% and clothing dropped 0.66%, while housing costs rose 0.99%. Expectations for Q1 2028, the bank’s relevant policy horizon, remained above the 3% target, and economists surveyed by the central bank expected 3.8% inflation at the end of 2028.

The minutes emphasized that deanchored expectations require greater restraint for longer than would otherwise be necessary. The bank also identified oil volatility and El Niño-related food risks as possible sources of second-round effects. Goldman Sachs economist Alberto Ramos regarded the mid-September meeting as open to another cut, but saw limited room for substantial near-term accommodation.

Kenya left its benchmark at 8.75% for a third meeting, matching all five forecasts in a survey. Governor Kamau Thugge said the stance was intended to keep inflation expectations inside the 2.5%-to-7.5% target range and stabilize the currency. The bank’s near-term inflation projection assumes that the Middle East conflict de-escalates, making the policy outlook directly conditional on an event that had not occurred by the US close.

Kenyan inflation rose to 6.5% in July from 6.4%, while core inflation increased to 3.2% from 3.1% as higher fuel costs spread into food and transport. A failed corn crop and the prospect of a strong El Niño add domestic supply risks. The central bank said it would monitor oil prices and second-round effects and was prepared to act if necessary.

The Philippines faces a simultaneous increase in fiscal supply and exposure to imported energy. The government plans to borrow 3.3 trillion pesos, or $54 billion, in 2027, about 20% more than this year’s revised 2.73 trillion-peso plan. Borrowing would finance 46% of a proposed 7.2 trillion-peso budget, which is 6% larger than the current allocation.

Domestic issuance is planned at 2.39 trillion pesos, up 24%, and would account for about 72% of total borrowing. The government expects to raise 915 billion pesos from foreign creditors, including multilateral lenders, with 366 billion pesos from international bonds compared with 314.4 billion pesos this year. It has already issued $5.25 billion of global bonds in 2026.

The fiscal deficit is projected at 1.69 trillion pesos, or 5.1% of GDP, above the previous 4.8% target. Outstanding debt stood at 19.07 trillion pesos in June, roughly 66% of GDP. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is increasing infrastructure and social spending and providing household tax relief and energy subsidies after the Iran war and a domestic corruption scandal weakened growth. Local bonds had already produced a 5% hedged dollar loss this year, while the peso was down 3.7%, leaving the larger supply plan to compete with inflation and currency risks.

The yen again weakened toward 160 per dollar, reviving speculation about intervention without materially changing the policy constraints. The currency had surrendered nearly half of the gain from the July 31 coordinated US-Japan operation. With the Bank of Japan rate at 1% and the Fed target at 3.5% to 3.75%, the interest-rate gap, Japan’s fiscal outlook and higher imported-energy costs continued to oppose the official preference for a stronger currency.

## Forward Market Significance

Wednesday’s July CPI release is the immediate test of the Treasury rally. The median forecast calls for a 0.1% monthly increase after a 0.4% decline, while one projection expects energy to subtract 11 basis points and core annual inflation to reach its lowest reading since March 2021. A broadly soft result would add domestic disinflation to the weak employment signal and could force covering among CTAs carrying record bond shorts. A result driven mainly by earlier energy declines, with persistent core services pressure, would offer less reason to abandon expectations of a September increase.

The distribution of the move across real yields and breakevens will matter. Both components of the 10-year nominal yield declined Tuesday even as oil rose. A benign CPI composition could extend that relief by reducing both the expected policy path and inflation compensation. A broad upside surprise would challenge the decline in the real yield and show that the oil shock is arriving before domestic persistence has sufficiently faded.

Hormuz requires operational evidence rather than another statement about negotiating progress. A durable change would include accepted passage terms, a timetable for reopening, sufficient traffic for commercial users and insurance conditions that allow ordinary shipments to resume. Iran’s insistence that the strait remain closed, despite Pakistan’s optimism, leaves those conditions unmet. The fall in average Q2 traffic to 4.9 million barrels a day from 21.6 million before the war gives the market a physical benchmark against which any agreement can be judged.

Thursday’s $25 billion 30-year Treasury auction will test demand near a 5.24% market yield after 41 sessions above 5%. Barclays expects the private and price-sensitive share of the buyer base to require structurally greater compensation for inflation, fiscal deficits and duration supply. The auction’s yield, bidding distribution and subsequent trading will show whether the current level attracts sufficient demand or still requires a larger concession.

Gainwell’s bond and loan are expected to complete later in the week. Roughly $4 billion of preliminary orders must translate into final pricing for a $4.34 billion package while investors assess AI disruption, the refinancing of the full capital structure and the value of the company’s improved operating results. Execution without significantly weaker terms would demonstrate capacity for a single-B software borrower; a smaller deal or larger concessions would reinforce the selectivity already visible across leveraged technology financing.

Nvidia’s emerging financing vehicles present a longer-running credit test. The company has clarified that its own support will be limited to as much as 25% of individual opportunities, but the first transactions must establish leverage, collateral rights, customer obligations and the treatment of obsolete or redeployed compute. The ability to raise tens of billions through special-purpose issuers will depend not only on Nvidia’s residual support but on whether project cash flows can service debt while physical construction and commercial returns catch up with capital commitments.

The Bank of Korea’s Aug. 27 meeting will determine whether persistent core inflation, strong exports and above-forecast growth justify another increase after July’s move to 2.75%. Revised growth and inflation forecasts will carry particular weight because Ryoo made the timing and pace of tightening conditional on that information. Australia, Brazil and Kenya have retained their own conditional biases, but Korea presents the nearest decision in which another hike is already an active possibility rather than a distant response to renewed pressure.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries edge higher before CPI despite another oil advance
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries edged higher on Aug. 11 as investors paused before July CPI despite a fifth consecutive oil advance. The 2-year yield fell 2.7 basis points to 4.216%, the 10-year eased 1.8 basis points to 4.69% and the 30-year declined 1.1 basis points to 5.242%, leaving the curve steeper. Both the 10-year real yield and breakeven inflation slipped, indicating that the session did not produce a broad repricing toward faster inflation.

The restraint reflected uncertainty over both domestic prices and energy supply. Economists expect headline CPI to rise 0.1% in July after a 0.4% decline, while record global-bond shorts could amplify the market response. Oil rose as Iran maintained that the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until its demands were met, despite Pakistan's claim that an arrangement was close; traffic through the strait had already fallen sharply from prewar levels.

Credit markets continued to absorb large transactions selectively. ICE sold $3.75 billion of acquisition financing, Blue Owl increased its offering after strong demand, and Gainwell launched a more difficult $4.34 billion refinancing package. Nvidia bonds strengthened after the company clarified that support for its proposed AI-financing platform would be limited to as much as 25% of individual opportunities rather than the $500 billion headline amount.
overall_summary.summary: Treasury yields declined modestly, led by the front end, as investors awaited July CPI rather than treating higher oil and unresolved Hormuz disruption as evidence that domestic inflation was accelerating.
